usage:

commands:

          [--acceptance-criteria TEXT] [--evidence-run-id RUN] [--evidence-fingerprint FP] [--evidence-artifact PATH]... [--worktree PATH] [--branch NAME]
          [--session ID]... [--pull-request PR]... [--assoc-branch B]... [--assoc-worktree PATH]... [--deferred] [--defer-reason R] [--defer-review-by DATE]   (a re-detected finding is REFUSED with exit 2)
  update  <id> --status complete [--title T] [--priority P1] [--worker-status S]
          [--commit-hash SHA] [--record-debt] [--guard PASS|FAIL|SKIP] [--ci GREEN|RED|SKIP]
          [--summary S] [--note S (appends)] [--blocked-reason R] [--completed-at TS]
          [--replace] [--worktree PATH] [--branch NAME] [--session ID]...
          [--acceptance-criteria TEXT]
          [--pull-request PR]... [--assoc-branch B]... [--assoc-worktree PATH]...
          (repeatable; each merges one element into its pull_requests/
          branches/worktrees dimension — existing elements, the other
          dimensions, and the singular worktree/branch fields survive)
          [--evidence-run-id RUN] [--evidence-fingerprint FP] [--evidence-artifact PATH]... [--deferred true|false] [--defer-reason R] [--defer-review-by DATE] [--normalize] [--force]
          [--initiative SLUG | --clear-initiative]
          (--initiative scopes the row into a programme and prints/rolls up under
          'initiatives'; --clear-initiative REMOVES the key, leaving no empty
          string to filter on. Together they are a usage error, not a precedence
          rule. Comparison on read is case-insensitive; writes store lowercase.)
          (--status complete REQUIRES --evidence-run-id: a completion without a
          bound run is REFUSED — TR-251; doctor reports the historic debt as
          verified_complete_share)
  event   --type task_created|task_dispatched|task_completed|audit|...
          [--task-id ID] [--actor foreman] [--detail @file | --detail-text '...']
          [--tick N] [--no-tick-write]
  header  [--json] [--set-ticks-total N] [--set-ticks-idle N] [--set-last-commit SHA] [--set-last-tick TIMESTAMP]
  validate [--skip-bad-lines] [--repair] [--strict-keys] [--fail-on dangling-dep]
  sweep-status [--apply] [--decide] [--json] [--skip-bad-lines]
           report (and with --apply fix) off-vocabulary task statuses on ONE
           board: known read aliases are normalized to their canonical form;
           unknown statuses (duplicate, parked, ...) are NEVER guessed — they
           are reported with the explicit decision needed. --decide adds the
           machine-checkable decisions: off-vocab guard/ci prose maps by rule
           (first token PASS|OK->PASS, FAIL|ERROR->FAIL, GREEN->GREEN,
           RED->RED; standalone SKIP or N/A -> SKIP; standalone SUCCESS ->
           GREEN on ci / PASS on guard; PENDING, ambiguous PASS+FAIL prose
           and anything unmatched stays explicit), and a status "duplicate"
           WITH an earlier same-id twin closes as superseded-by-earliest
           (--apply only; one audit event quotes the preserved text);
           a "duplicate" with no earlier twin is refused. --decide alone
           never writes; only --decide --apply does.
  normalize-statuses [--apply] [--dry-run] [--json] [-C dir]
           report status aliases and unknown/missing values on ONE resolved board;
           dry-run is the default and never writes; --apply atomically canonicalizes
           known aliases only, while unknown/missing statuses remain refused.
  normalize-board [--apply] [--repair-events] [--json]
           report (and with --apply fix) drifted row SHAPES on ONE board —
           the board-wide twin of 'update --normalize': renames known key
           aliases to their canonical keys, converts string depends_on

           values to arrays where the conversion is unambiguous ("[]" and
           "" -> [], a JSON array string -> the array, one bare id ->
           [id]), and canonicalizes alias statuses (open -> pending). Rows
           needing a human decision are REFUSED and reported: an alias over
           a key the row already carries, an unconvertible depends_on shape
           (number/object/malformed), a status that is absent/null/unknown.
           Rows without created_at are counted and reported — never
           fabricated. DRY-RUN by default: stages the would-be bytes at
           <boarddir>/tasks.normalized.jsonl for review; --apply rewrites
           tasks.jsonl in ONE guarded atomic pass (all repairs or nothing).

  doctor
  evidence baseline --record   record completion debt and enable FAIL-on-new-debt
  version [--json]
  stats   [--json] [--all] [--skip-bad-lines]
  initiatives [--json] [--status S] [--skip-bad-lines]   list initiative rollups on this board

  import  <export.json> [--dry-run] [--renumber]
  serve   [-C dir] [--addr 127.0.0.1:8787]

          [--fleet PAT] [--fleet-root DIR] [--lint-mode enforce|warn]

          hook across every git repo under --fleet-root (default ~) matching
          the comma-separated glob-or-path list PAT, one outcome line per
          repo (installed / already present / skipped-no-board /
          skipped-no-binary / skipped / FAILED + why); a worktree checkout
          (.git is a file) is skipped — its hook lives in the main checkout;
          --lint-mode sets the reject-arm behavior on a boardctl validate
          failure: enforce (default) blocks the commit, warn prints the
          same evidence behind a WARN-ONLY banner and allows it (a
          re-install flips the mode in place; --fleet carries the mode
          into every hook it writes)
  hook    install|uninstall|doctor|dispatch|flush
          install --hook <post-commit|post-merge> --crier-url URL --secret-file PATH
          [--source-id ID] [--self BIN] [--hook-path P] [--dry-run];
          uninstall --hook <post-commit|post-merge> [--hook-path P];
          doctor [--probe-timeout 2s];
          dispatch --hook <post-commit|post-merge> [--crier-url URL] [--secret-file PATH]
          [--source-id ID] [--batch-cap N] [--budget 10s] [--dry-run];
          flush [--dry-run]
          git-hook intake for the crier pipeline (BOARDCTL-HOOK-001). install
          appends a delimited managed block to .git/hooks/<hook> (never
          replacing a sibling body); uninstall removes ONLY that block and
          restores the pre-install bytes exactly. dispatch diffs HEAD^..HEAD
          (post-commit) or ORIG_HEAD..HEAD (post-merge), and POSTs each newly
          added/seen pending row to <crier-url>/ingress/webhooks/<source-id>
          signed with X-Crier-Timestamp + sha256=HMAC(secret, timestamp.body)
          and Idempotency-Key boardctl:<row-id>:<content-hash> (the hash
          excludes the row id). It NEVER blocks the commit: every failure exits
          0, undelivered rows spool beside the board and, after 3 attempts,
          become an operator-visible dead-letter record. doctor names every
          failing condition (exit 1); flush drains the spool on demand.
  umbrella [--list|--stats|--validate] [--status s1,s2] [--json] [--strict]
           [--skip-bad-lines] [-C dir]
          read-only unified view over this repo and every child board
          symlinked under .coding-hermes/links/ (one symlink per child
          repo, named after the repo, aimed at <child>/.coding-hermes).
          --status filters the --list task table (comma-separated
          statuses; aliases like done/todo normalize).
          Tasks keep repo provenance; ids are repo-qualified (<repo>/<id>),
          colliding ids stay distinct, and cross-board depends_on refs
          resolve only when unambiguous (AMBIGUOUS is reported, never
          guessed). Broken/looping/out-of-repo links are findings (exit 1),
          never followed. NEVER writes — writes stay single-repo via -C.
          Line-level reads: by default the FIRST unparseable line in any
          board aborts the whole view (exit 1, no partial output);
          --skip-bad-lines degrades instead — every parseable row from
          every healthy board is still counted/listed, each unparseable
          line is reported on stderr as a SKIPPED-LINES block naming its
          board and file:line, and the command exits 1

--skip-bad-lines (list/show/stats/validate/render/umbrella): read the board
tolerantly, keeping every line that parses; unparseable lines are reported on
stderr as a SKIPPED-LINES evidence block and the command exits 1 even though it
produced its normal output. Without the flag the first unparseable line aborts.
For umbrella the block names each skipped line's board + file:line and the
parseable rows of every healthy child board are still counted/listed.
validate --repair: salvage every parseable row into <boarddir>/tasks.rewritten.jsonl
(manual review file — tasks.jsonl is never overwritten).
validate --strict-keys: treat BT-056 key-uniformity drift as an error (exit 1).
validate --fail-on dangling-dep: treat a dangling depends_on reference (a
warning by default) as a failure (exit 1). The pre-commit hook installed by
'boardctl install' passes this flag; plain validate stays exit 0.
Every validate run prints the census line "key uniformity: N/M rows carry only
canon keys" — quote it as evidence of zero drift.

-C resolves the board dir: a repo root (looks for .coding-hermes/board),
.coding-hermes, or the board dir itself. Defaults to the current directory.
